record.context_brief: Polynomial-time proper learning of decision trees
record.original_question: Does there exist a membership-query algorithm that runs in time polynomial in the number of variables n, the target decision-tree size s, and 1/epsilon, and that properly learns any size-s decision tree over {0,1}^n to error at most epsilon under the uniform distribution? The learner should output a decision-tree hypothesis, and the problem remains open even if the learner is allowed to be only weakly proper, meaning it may return a decision tree whose size is not restricted to s.

evidence.quote: The main open problem of this article is the following: Open Problem 1 Design a poly(n, s, 1/epsilon)-time membership query algorithm for properly learning size-s decision trees over n variables to error epsilon under the uniform distribution.

We also mention here the distinction between a strictly proper versus weakly proper algorithm: the former returns a size-s decision tree hypothesis for a size-s target, whereas the latter can return a decision tree of any size. Open Problem 1 is open even for weakly proper algorithms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\epsilon\in(0,1)$. A decision tree over the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ is a rooted binary tree in which each internal node is labeled by a variable $x_i$, has two outgoing edges labeled $0$ and $1$, and each leaf is labeled by a value in $\{0,1\}$; the tree computes a Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ in the natural way. The size of a decision tree is its number of leaves. A learning algorithm with membership queries has black-box query access to an unknown target function $f$ (i.e., on input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ it receives $f(x)$); it is said to properly learn size-$s$ decision trees under the uniform distribution to error $\epsilon$ if, for every $f$ computable by a decision tree of size at most $s$, the algorithm outputs (with high probability) a decision tree hypothesis $h$ such that $\Pr_{x\sim\{0,1\}^n}[h(x)\neq f(x)]\le\epsilon$. The algorithm is called strictly proper if $h$ is required to have size at most $s$, and weakly proper if $h$ is allowed to be any decision tree (of unrestricted size).

Question: Does there exist a membership-query algorithm running in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,s,1/\epsilon)$ that properly learns size-$s$ decision trees over $\{0,1\}^n$ under the uniform distribution to error at most $\epsilon$? The problem is to be settled even in the weakly proper setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known algorithm for properly learning size-$s$ decision trees under the uniform distribution with membership queries runs in quasi-polynomial time $n^{O(\log\log n)}$ (Blanc, Lange, Qiao, Tan, JACM 2022), improving the long-standing $n^{O(\log n)}$ bound of Ehrenfeucht–Haussler. No polynomial-time algorithm (even weakly proper) is known, and the question is explicitly posed as an open problem; no resolution has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Properly Learning Decision Trees in almost Polynomial Time (JACM)
status_evidence.snippet: An n^{O(log log n)}-time membership query algorithm for properly and agnostically learning decision trees under the uniform distribution, improving on the previous fastest runtime of n^{O(log n)}.
status_evidence.claim: Current best runtime is quasi-polynomial, not polynomial.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Properly learning decision trees in polynomial time? (COLT 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: The natural open problem is obtaining a polynomial-time algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is explicitly posed as open.
